what: Hand-marked verdicts on every relation the reader produced over two deterministic slices of the Wikipedia corpus, and a per-article verdict on the definition of each article's own subject. Marked once, after the fixes the coverage run motivated.
how: A relation is right when it is a true copular predication of the subject recorded beside it. It is wrong when the object is a passive complement, a predicative adjective, a sentence fragment, a span crossing a sentence boundary, or when the subject it was filed under does not hold it. A kind is right when the head noun it names is the category the article's subject actually falls under; producing none counts as wrong.
